Now I'm free to execute an OSCLI call on the host to run the loader, which runs on the parasite. After checking which Tube side it's running on (omitted because we've already covered that) it starts with this.

In this case I'm detecting different CPU types for choosing whether to load an enhanced version of the program. This is one place where you need a 'proper' 65x assembler, not BeebAsm...unless you're prepared to use EQUB for parts of it.

Code: 

.pc02
.proc EntryPoint
	;	work out which CPU variant
	lda	#1

.p816
	;	this will only leave A as 0 after the 2nd XBA on 65C02
	xba
	dec	a
	xba
.pc02

	;	A = 
	;	0	65C02
	;	1	65816

entry.title: programming • Re: Writing games for the Tube: bare metal
entry.content:
The Tube host is a bit too big to be posting here, despite its slimmed down nature, but I'll share it in another way.

The important bits of the custom Tube host code are:

Only OSFILE is supported from the normal OS calls, so we can load and save settings or high scores or whatever.

In the &406 reason code handler executed on the host, in the Acorn one, the JMP at the end here isn't a thing (it's a JSR) and the next instruction returns the host to the tight loop running in ZP. This variation hands control back to the host after, say, a *RUN OSCLI call.

We are gradually eliminating the Acorn Tube protocol (or most of it).

The net result of this is that you can *RUN something that has a parasite execution address and it will do it. The parasite program will just get on with its job, initialisation or whatever. What is not then happening is the host waiting for OSWRCH calls or anything else (and at this point not even OSFILE)

Code: 

_noSendSyncByte
	cpx	#TUBE_ACTION_EXECUTE_IN_PARASITE
	bne	_noSendStartByte

	;	send start byte
	lda	#$80
	jmp	TubeHostWriteR2

_noSendStartByte
	rts

entry.title: 8-bit acorn hardware • Re: BeebSID
entry.content:
SID emulation for your BBC via Pi1MHZ!

If you don't have the BeebSID hardware, but do have a Pi1MHZ (or plan to get one), its firmware now emulates BeebSID as well!

From v1.30 - https://github.com/dp111/Pi1MHz/releases
Interesting! Does this mean that I don’t need to build a BeebSID? I have the bare PCBs on their way, but if the emulation is decent it might save me time and money. I was almost certainly going to use a SID replacement rather than a genuine one. I guess I will give the Pi1MHz a try.
Yes, its totally another option. The emulation library used is not these days considered the most accurate, but is the most compatible with the architecture of Pi1MHz. I personally have both and other than a bit less bass at times its perfectly good emulation and I have played some of the more tricky SIDs. So yes, I would say give it a go and see what your ears think - its certainly worth a try!
Thanks!

entry.title: programming • Re: Writing games for the Tube: bare metal
entry.content:
So, um TubeHostInstall is just a data transfer loop. I think the Tube host code would probably be more interesting. I can say, without even looking, though, that the bulk of the code lives at &400 as normal and ZP usage is 12 bytes - Acorn must have had their reasons for running code in ZP but I don't see any reason to do the same. Works fine.
I love the stripped-down simplicity of your setup. It’s so elegant!

To make the point even more, I think ZP usage for the Acorn host code is a fair amount more than 12 bytes. It seems to use pretty much the whole block from &0000 to &0056; sticking breakpoints on the code in here halts things all the time, particularly the block at &0036. So your approach is even slicker than you’re claiming. Nice.

Mark
I was wrong about 12. It's 11.

Code: 

ZP_TUBE_CLAIM_ID
	db	0

ZP_TUBE_CONTROL_BLOCK_POINTER
	dw	0

ZP_COMMAND_HOST_ADDRESS
	dw	0
ZP_COMMAND_LENGTH
	dw	0
ZP_COMMAND_PARASITE_ADDRESS
	dd	0

ZP_TUBE_HOST_TOP
.export ZP_TUBE_HOST_TOP
